key_insight: An inverse-designed selective emitter achieves a modeled 47.0% thermophotovoltaic efficiency by suppressing sub-bandgap radiation before it reaches the cell.
engineering_relevance: Emitter-side spectral control could reduce reliance on cell-side photon recycling while maintaining comparable maximum electrical power density.
method: Optimize a 16-layer aperiodic MgO/Si coating on tungsten.
Pair the emitter with a GaSb cell featuring an antireflection coating and Au mirror.
Model angle- and polarization-resolved emission, multiple reflections, and Auger recombination using detailed balance.
evidence_signal: At 1500 K, simulations show 97.1% source suppression of incident-blackbody-equivalent sub-bandgap power and 47.0% conversion efficiency, versus 30.8% for SiC with the same cell.
watch_item: Results are numerical; fabrication tolerances and multilayer stability at 1500 K require experimental validation.
paper_title: An Inverse-Designed Multilayer Selective Emitter for High-Efficiency Thermophotovoltaics
